plan: My private value is $9. In a first-price sealed bid auction, I want to bid strategically. Since the value is drawn randomly, I can't predict other bidders' values. A pure profit-maximizing strategy is to bid slightly less than my true value. I'll bid $8.9, which leaves me a small potential profit margin if I win. This approach protects against overbidding while still giving me a chance to acquire the item if my bid is competitive.

My private value is $20. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid your true value. This prevents underbidding (and potentially losing a profitable item) or overbidding (and potentially losing money). Since values are independently drawn, I can't predict others' values. Bidding $20 ensures I win if my value is higher than others, and only pay a price below my value if I win.
